text:
emily: hitting dup creates using AsyncClient when socket read times out. minimal repro below. sometimes two resources created.

tom: sync or async?

emily: AsyncClient, default retries=2, no Idempotency-Key set. repro:
```python
async with AsyncClient(api_key=\"sk\") as c:
    await c.post(\"/items\", json={\"name\":\"dup\"}, timeout=0.7)
```

vera: sounds like client timed out after server committed create, retried and server treated it as new. Server dedupe only by Idempotency-Key.

tom: then two issues: 1) should SDK offer auto-idempotency when retries are on? 2) Async typings are missing in stubs so callers can't type responses.

emily: +1 on both. For auto-idemp we should be conservative: only auto-generate for JSON POST/PUT with small content-length and only for in-flight retries (no cross-process caching).

vera: propose idempotency_strategy: \"explicit\" (default), \"auto\", \"none\". Auto opt-in via client param for patch release. Also add retry_on_timeout flag and jittered exp backoff.

tom: i'll add typed overloads for AsyncClient methods in stubs and a mypy check.

ci-bot: test run: repro_dup_create (emily/repro) -> 2/8 duplicates observed, logs attached.

docs-bot: filed INF-4401 with repro, logs, and suggested SDK change list.

emily: workaround: set Idempotency-Key header manually + increase timeout. Example: headers={\"Idempotency-Key\": uuid4().hex}

vera: agreed on opt-in for now. follow-ups: tom -> stubs, emily -> e2e test, vera -> design doc + docs note.

emily: thanks, filing PRs now.
